- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 20–40% for short-term (1–7d) horizons.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast lows by 15–30% for short-term horizons.
- Model consistently overreacts to sentiment spikes — if sentiment jumps >0.67 within 3d, reduce forecast overshoot by 50% for next 7d.
- For 30d forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if recent 18d mean is >1.5, cap forecast at 1.5–2.0 unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 10–20% to forecast for 1–7d horizon.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is mixed or negative, model tends to overpredict volatility — cap forecast at 3x recent 18d average unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >2.0 in any 7d window, apply downward correction proportional to sentiment magnitude (e.g., 0.5x sentiment value).
